Forehead
FOR-hed
noun
From the Saxon forheafod, “fore-head,” the front of the head above the eyes; rendering the Hebrew metsach, the brow, and the Greek metopon, that part of the face which cannot be hidden and which therefore carries whatever mark is set upon it.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The forehead in Scripture is the open face of a man — the one part of him that goes before him into every room and can conceal nothing. Because it cannot be hidden, it becomes the appointed place of allegiance. Upon the high priest’s brow was bound the golden plate engraved HOLINESS TO THE LORD, “always upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before the LORD” (Exo 28:38): the mediator wears the acceptance of the people where all may read it. When Ezekiel is sent to a rebellious house, the LORD hardens the prophet’s brow to match theirs — “As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead” (Eze 3:9) — not a stubborn heart, but a face that will not blush before scoffers. Set against this is Judah’s “whore’s forehead” (Jer 3:3), brazenness that has lost the very power of shame. And in judgment the brow is where God distinguishes His own: the mark set upon the men that sigh and cry for the abominations of the city (Eze 9:4), and the sealing of the servants of God in their foreheads before the winds are loosed (Rev 7:3). Satan can only counterfeit; the mark in the right hand or in the forehead (Rev 13:16) is the devil’s parody of a seal he cannot make. Two brows, two owners, and no third party: every man is publicly marked, and the mark is read by God before it is read by men.

Webster 1828 Definition

The front of the head above the eyes; hence the open, unhidden part of a man, and in Scripture the appointed place of a mark, a plate, or a seal declaring whose he is.

FOREHEAD, n. The part of the face which extends from the hair on the top of the head to the eyes.

From fore and head; Saxon forheafod.

Impudence; audaciousness; assurance; as in a brazen or a whore’s forehead (Jer 3:3).

The place appointed for the high priest’s golden plate, engraven HOLINESS TO THE LORD (Exo 28:36–38).

In prophetic Scripture, the place of a distinguishing mark or seal (Eze 9:4; Rev 7:3; 13:16).

Key Scripture

Eze 3:9 — "As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead: fear them not, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they be a rebellious house."

Eze 9:4 — "And the LORD said unto him, Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof."

Exo 28:38 — "And it shall be upon Aaron's forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things, which the children of Israel shall hallow in all their holy gifts; and it shall be always upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before the LORD."

Rev 7:3 — "Saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads."

Modern Corruption

Rev 13:16’s mark in the forehead has been turned into a barcode-and-microchip spectacle by dispensational date-setting, which reads a sign of open allegiance as a technology and sells the reading in paperbacks.

expand to see more

The corruption is sensationalism. Since Darby and Scofield in the nineteenth century, and industrially since the 1970s, dispensational premillennialism has taught readers to hunt the mark of the beast among credit cards, national identity numbers, implanted chips, and whatever technology is newest at the printing of the book. Every generation of that literature has named its candidate, every generation’s candidate has aged into embarrassment, and the church has been trained to read Revelation as a puzzle about hardware rather than a comfort about the Lamb. The dictionary rejects dispensational premillennialism outright as a novelty absent from every Reformation confession, and rejects its handling of this text in particular. Note what the sensational reading destroys: it severs Rev 13:16 from Rev 7:3, which it plainly answers. The sealing of the servants of God in their foreheads comes first; the mark in the right hand or in the forehead is the imitation. Satan is not an inventor, he is a forger, and a forgery is only intelligible next to the genuine article — the priestly plate on Aaron’s brow, the ink-mark of Eze 9:4, the seal of the Spirit on the believer.

Recover the plain sense: the forehead is where allegiance is public. The hand is what a man does and the forehead is what a man openly is, and Scripture marks both because a man serves with his labour and confesses with his face. To be sealed in the forehead is to belong to God visibly and irrevocably, and no one who reads Eze 9:4 will think the mark is placed on the indifferent: it is set on the men that sigh and that cry over the abominations of the city, that is, upon the grieving remnant. Two practical consequences follow. First, the believer’s comfort in an evil day is not that he will outwit a numbering system but that he is already sealed. Second, the believer’s duty is Ezekiel’s — a brow made adamant, a face that will not colour before a rebellious house. Brazenness that cannot blush (Jer 3:3) and boldness that will not flinch look alike to the world and are opposites before God; the difference is entirely whose name is written on the brow.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The unhidden front of the head; hence the appointed place of a plate, a mark, or a seal, declaring openly whose a man is.

expand to see more

Forehead — Saxon forheafod, the fore part of the head.

Hebrew metsach, the brow (Exo 28:38; Eze 3:9; Jer 3:3).

Greek metopon, literally “between the eyes” (Rev 7:3; 13:16).

Because it cannot be hidden, it is the biblical site of open allegiance.

The mark of Rev 13:16 is the counterfeit of the seal of Rev 7:3, not its original.

Usage

"The high priest bore acceptance on his brow (Exo 28:38) — Christ bears ours where all may read it."

"Ezekiel’s adamant forehead is courage, not obstinacy; Jeremiah’s whore’s forehead is shamelessness."

"Read the mark of Rev 13:16 backwards from Rev 7:3: forgery presupposes an original seal."
